title: Check every part and every version
statement: Check every line a student reads, passages, options, keys, definitions and every rewrite, for the subject's known misconceptions, flagging hits in code before publication whoever wrote it.
example: In one unit, the lesson sweeps found a misconception outside the passage three times: in a keyed answer, a check option and a taught word's definition.
detail: A science synthesis asks for its absolute prohibitions, such as saying energy is used up, to be automated checks on any content made for the curriculum, whether by people or AI (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Cross-Cutting Synthesis.docx`), and the coherence guidance sends all science-related text through the misconception check (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Brainlift social science and science coherence.md`). In one unit, the lesson sweeps changed a keyed answer from plants making energy from sunlight to plants making food (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.2 - The Living World - Lesson Designs/3.2 - 1. The Wonderful World of Plants - FIND - Lesson Design (v2 - MCQ pauses + science sweep).docx`), reworded a check option and redefined a taught word, while other sweeps found nothing to fix. A comparison made in this run found a draft science text and its rewrite byte-identical, both still saying the rest of the energy is lost as heat or used up (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/G4 DRAFT/Rewrites/2. Ecosystems and Food Webs - rewrite.docx`). The check covers phrasing known to teach a misconception as well as the misconception itself.
against: the draft text and its rewrite both sit in a draft folder and may not yet have reached the check (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/G4 DRAFT/2. Ecosystems and Food Webs.docx`).
